name: Ephraim
overview: Ephraim is a male figure known as the second son of Joseph, belonging to the tribe named after him, Ephraim. His unique attribute is being the younger son of Joseph and Asenath, born in Egypt. There are no additional notes provided about his personal characteristics.
namesAndTitles: The name Ephraim means 'doubly fruitful,' reflecting a theme of blessing and productivity. This proper name is not explicitly given by God but is recorded in Scripture, indicating his identity and role within the family lineage.
familyAndRelationships: Ephraim is explicitly recorded as the son of Joseph and Asenath. He is also an ancestor to several individuals and families mentioned in the Old Testament, including Ammihud, Nun, and others inferred through genealogies. These relationships establish Ephraim as a patriarchal figure within the tribe that bears his name.
scriptureSignificance: Ephraim's significance lies in his position as the younger son who received a greater blessing from Jacob, highlighting God's sovereign choice in elevating the younger over the elder. His descendants formed the dominant tribe in northern Israel, and the name Ephraim became synonymous with the northern kingdom. This prominence fulfills the divine blessing and plays a key role in Israel's history, even as the tribe later led the nation into idolatry.

keyEvents.event: Blessed by Jacob, received right hand
